resources.string: Dictator listens only while you dictate, and transcribes on this phone. Audio is never saved.
Allow Dictator to draw a floating microphone over other apps. Your keyboard stays as it is.
Turn on Dictator under Accessibility. It types into the field you are in, and reads only that field so the words land at the cursor. Nothing is stored.
One microphone. It appears when a text field is focused. Tap to start and stop, hold to talk, drag to move it.

Dictator is not a keyboard, so it never replaces the one you type with. Audio stays on this phone. The button reads the focused text field, in memory, only to place the dictation. It never uses the clipboard.

Types dictated speech into the text field you are using. Dictator reads that field so the words land at the cursor, with the right spacing. It does not read the rest of the screen, and it stores nothing.
Tap here, then tap the floating microphone.
Audio never leaves the device; the one-time model download is the only network use. MIT licensed.
Allow the microphone in Dictator to dictate.
Tap to toggle · Hold to talk
Release to finish, or tap again
The microphone appears in a text field

Turn on Dictator under Accessibility so it can type into the field.

%1$s is downloaded and ready. Dictation works offline.
Dictator needs the %1$s speech model (%2$s MB), downloaded once. Wi-Fi is recommended.
Waiting for Wi-Fi (or a connection) to download the model…
The one-time model download from Hugging Face is the only network use. Every file is checked against a SHA-256 hash built into the app. Your audio never leaves the device.
